source.title: Exploring Unsupervised Methods for Recovering the Refusal Direction in LLMs

record.file_problem: The post is present, but equations, direction labels, and figures are missing or stripped in the supplied text. Some results are therefore only described qualitatively, and two Qwen values cannot be matched to their direction labels.
record.tranche_reason: It applies directional ablation and measures refusal suppression and KL divergence, using the difference-in-means approach on new instruct models. It also compares PCA and Isomap directions.
record.gate_note: The text reports direction comparisons, ablation efficacy, KL divergence, and held-out classification/geometry results. Most plotted values are unavailable in the supplied text. Classification of prompts as harmful or harmless is not itself a model refusal rate.
record.test_reason: It ablates difference-in-means (and PCA-recovered) refusal directions in Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct and Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct. It measures refusal bypass on harmful prompts and KL divergence on harmless prompts, the original V1 method and measures on new models.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly correct. The authors conclude that PCA recovers a direction directionally and causally similar to the diff-in-means refusal direction, and that it works as a harmful/harmless classifier with modest sample sizes. They also conclude that Isomap shows no curved-manifold structure and performs worse than PCA.
record.recipe_differences: Uses difference-in-means and causal ablation, while adding PCA and Isomap recovery methods. Uses BeaverTails for fitting harmful prompts rather than the original harmful dataset; tests Llama 3.1 8B Instruct and Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct.
record.method_sensitivity: For Qwen, L20 is selected because no layer met both the stated KL and bypass thresholds; the text reports KL divergence of 0.133 and 0.197 for two directions. Layer-specific plots are unavailable in the supplied text.

fits_no_version.finding: PCA's first component recovers a direction with high cosine similarity to the diff-in-means refusal direction, even with modest n and imbalanced classes (20-90% harmful). Projection onto it classifies held-out harmful vs harmless prompts.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: The refusal direction can be recovered without labels, as the dominant variance axis of harmful+harmless activations.

fits_no_version.finding: Isomap's first coordinate correlates linearly with projection onto the refusal direction and performs worse than PCA, giving no sign of a curved manifold.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Refusal-related activation geometry is linear rather than lying on a curved manifold.

record.problems: The supplied text omits the figures and much of the mathematical notation. Most plotted values, layer mappings, and direction labels cannot be read. The post gives no uncertainty estimates. Its capability check is KL divergence on harmless prompts, and the author notes the <0.1 KL threshold is arbitrary.
record.rows_left_out: No results were left out beyond the unavailable plotted information; the supplied text does not provide recoverable values for the omitted figures.

untested.parts: Adding the direction to induce refusal on harmless prompts. Broad capability benchmarks (only harmless-prompt KL is reported). Llama ablation and KL values are figure-only and cannot be read.

missing.what: Statement that no Qwen layer satisfied both KL <0.1 and bypass >0.80, i.e. the layer-selection tradeoff. It is currently only in method_sensitivity, not a row.
Sweep-n and imbalanced-class PCA results (figure/repo only).

record.verdict_notes: Figures and direction symbols are stripped, so the Llama results cannot be read. The only readable numbers are Qwen L20. Commenters note that PC1 recovering the class-mean difference is expected. Informal LessWrong post with no uncertainty estimates.

versions.untested_parts: The study does not test adding the direction to induce refusals on harmless prompts. Its capability evidence is limited to KL divergence on harmless prompts, not a broad assessment of other abilities.
